title: Breast Implant Rippling and Bottoming Out: Causes, Fixes
meta_description: Rippling: implant folds felt or seen through skin, 0.7% to 13.7% in the augmentation figures we found. Bottoming out: an implant settling too low.
excerpt: Rippling and bottoming out are different problems with different causes, and neither has one reliable rate. Here's what raises the odds, how placement and implant type connect, what a fix usually involves, and what the evidence can't tell you.
quick_answer:
What causes breast implant rippling and bottoming out?

Rippling is wrinkling of the implant that shows or can be felt through the skin, the FDA says, and Allergan's labeling says it may be more likely with saline. Bottoming out means the implant settles too low. The FDA says implants can shift from gravity, trauma or capsular contracture. Correcting either usually means another operation.

Search Console shows only single impressions on these queries (window above), so its data set the wording of the H2s and FAQs, not demand or rank. cta stays default: the breast CTA in apps/web/lib/data/blog-cta-content.ts says 'our board-certified surgeons' and carries a phone number, which compliance forbids, so no marker. No practice price, placement, incision or implant brand is stated; cost links to the procedure page #pricing per the plan's practice-question default. Fat grafting and acellular dermal matrix appear only as options a 2018 paper lists, not as anything the practice offers. Thin evidence stated in the post: no study followed rippling over time; no comparison of fixes; bottoming out has only one center's figure; makers report malposition, not bottoming out. Sources read beyond SOURCE-BANK on 2026-11-03: PubMed abstracts 29546437, 30483933, 16991043, 34297171; The Aesthetic Society breast revision page; Caplin full text for the mild-excluded footnote; Sientra and Allergan PDFs for table context (revision rows, reasons for reoperation, thin-tissue lines). Hoch and Stahlenbrecher is a German-language paper read through its English PubMed abstract. Links to N1, N2, N3, N4 are new posts in the same batch and must go live in the same run or be swapped. Allergan's reconstruction figure and the weight-lifting FAQ were cut for length. Fact check batch6 decisions applied on 2026-11-03: the stretched lower breast and high nipple description is labeled as practical advice and no longer attributed to the 2006 paper; the rippling range is limited to the augmentation figures; the rupture FAQ says Sientra does not tie shell folding to visible rippling.
